drivingQuestion: Under what conditions is an animal whose lower jaw was removed still kosher?
outcomeNote: A single amoraic qualification of the mishna, unchallenged.

segments.he: נִיטַּל לֶחִי הַתַּחְתּוֹן, אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁיְּכוֹלָה לִחְיוֹת עַל יְדֵי לְעִיטָה וְהַמְרָאָה, אֲבָל אֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לִחְיוֹת עַל יְדֵי לְעִיטָה וְהַמְרָאָה – טְרֵפָה.
segments.en: § The mishna states: If the animal’s «lower jaw was removed,» it remains kosher. With regard to this, «Rabbi Zeira says:» The Sages «taught» this «only when» the animal «is able to live by placing» food in its mouth «or stuffing» it down its throat. «But» if «it cannot live by placing or stuffing» food into it, it is «a tereifa.»

moves.summary: quotes the mishna's ruling on a removed lower jaw
moves.about: quoting the mishna's ruling that an animal whose lower jaw was removed remains kosher

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי זירא: לא שנו אלא
moves.summary: restricts the leniency to an animal that can still live by force-feeding
moves.about: the mishna's leniency holds only where the animal can still live by force-feeding; otherwise it is a tereifa
